children.content: Northbridge Building Society · Board risk committee

children.name: Subtitle
children.content: Findings and recommendations from a six-week review

children.name: Lede
children.content: Where staff use AI today, and what leaves the building with it.

children.name: Headline
children.content: Most AI use bypasses the controls you already run

children.name: Lede
children.content: Staff in four of six departments use generative AI every week. Few of those tools went through procurement or security review.

children.name: Body
children.content: The acceptable use policy predates these tools and does not name them. Data loss rules do not inspect prompts, so member data leaves without a record.

children.name: Fact 1
children.content: 14 AI tools found in proxy logs; 11 never reviewed.

children.name: Fact 2
children.content: 38% of 400 sampled prompts held member data.

children.name: Source
children.content: Source: proxy logs and prompt sample, September 2026.

children.name: Headline
children.content: Four actions close the largest gaps by March

children.name: Action
children.content: Name an executive owner for AI risk

children.name: Reason
children.content: Decisions about AI stop falling between three functions.

children.name: Action
children.content: Route every AI tool through one review

children.name: Reason
children.content: New tools reach staff only after security and data checks.

children.name: Action
children.content: Inspect prompts with data loss rules

children.name: Reason
children.content: Member data in prompts is blocked or logged, not lost.

children.name: Reason
children.content: An outside view confirms the controls hold.

children.name: Headline
children.content: Three gaps carry most of the risk

children.name: Lede
children.content: Each one is fixable with controls Northbridge already owns; none needs a new platform.

children.name: Claim
children.content: 11 of 14 tools in use were never reviewed

children.name: Body
children.content: Staff adopted them faster than procurement could respond, mostly through browser extensions.

children.name: Body
children.content: 38% of 400 sampled prompts held names, account numbers or addresses.

children.name: Claim
children.content: No one owns AI risk at board level

children.name: Body
children.content: Decisions fall between IT, data protection and risk, so none of them is made.

children.name: Headline
children.content: Two decisions shape the next six months

children.name: Lede
children.content: Both sit with the board; the rest of the programme follows from them.

children.name: Claim
children.content: Approve tools centrally, not team by team

children.name: Body
children.content: One review gate costs less than eleven separate exceptions and closes the shadow AI gap.

children.name: Claim
children.content: Fund prompt inspection this financial year

children.name: Body
children.content: Existing data loss tooling covers it with a licence change; no new platform is needed.

children.name: Statement
children.content: Northbridge can keep using AI safely if it reviews tools before staff adopt them.

children.name: Body
children.content: Most use came through browser extensions and features switched on in software Northbridge already licenses.

children.name: Body 2
children.content: No one decided to adopt AI. It was already there.

children.name: Headline
children.content: One review gate for every new AI tool

dNoteT.content: Every rejection names an approved alternative.

children.name: Headline
children.content: Gaps are widest where AI meets member data
